disagreements: The packet says the midpoint-ball normal cone is 'byte-identical logic in all seven modules'. The computation is behaviourally identical in all seven (same rho=.sup(), same cn=.inf(), same refusal, same (1+8eps) ulp nudge, same PI clamp), but two of the seven spell the guard with the clauses in a different order: extruded.rs and revolved.rs wrote `if cn <= rho || !cn.is_finite() || !rho.is_finite()`, the other five wrote `if !cn.is_finite() || !rho.is_finite() || cn <= rho`. A pure OR of side-effect-free predicates is identical on every input (including NaN), so this is not a behavioural divergence, but the packet's 'byte-identical' wording is not literally accurate. The shared `crate::enclosure::midpoint_ball_cone` uses the packet's prescribed form.
